version.changelog: Initial release: grade how vibe-coded a codebase is, with a report card and copy-paste fix-it prompts.

llm.summary: This skill is a local code-quality report generator with disclosed repo scanning, report-file writes, and localhost serving; its broad activation wording is worth noticing but does not show malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to grade a codebase and produce a report, and the artifacts support that with a deterministic scanner, scoring references, report builder, and localhost report server.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The frontmatter asks agents to use the skill for broad intents like audit, code quality score, roast, report card, and code smells even when unnamed, which could make it handle some generic review requests more aggressively than a user expected.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The README describes a standard copy or symlink skill install and requires Node 18+; runtime scripts are bundled and dependency-free, with no npm install required for normal use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scanner reads recognized code files in the target repo, honors common ignore directories and simple .gitignore entries, caps large walks, and showed no network upload or credential/session access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: A run writes .slop-check metrics, a slop map, report data, and slop-report.html, then may start a localhost-only server; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no evidence of hidden long-term persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this if you want generic code-quality, audit, or code-smell requests to produce a slop-check report. Be aware it will read the target repo, write local report artifacts into the repo, and may start a localhost report server; avoid invoking it on repositories containing secrets you do not want summarized into local report files.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger language is real and users should understand it, but the resulting behavior is still the advertised local repo scan and report workflow; it is not hidden exfiltration, destructive action, or unrelated privilege use.
